cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Diyas – small oil lamps made of clay, traditionally used during Diwali.

p.em: Example: Lighting diyas symbolizes the victory of light over darkness.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rangoli – an art form in which patterns are created on the floor using materials such as colored rice, flour, or flower petals.

p.em: Example: Creating a beautiful rangoli at the entrance of the house welcomes guests and good luck.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prosperity ≠ poverty – the state of being successful, especially in material or financial terms.

p.em: Example: Diwali is a time to pray for prosperity and health for the coming year.

cosy-blockquote.p: Festivity – the celebration of something in a very happy and exciting way.

p.em: Example: The streets were filled with music and general festivity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Firecrackers – small explosive devices used primarily to produce a large amount of noise.

p.em: Example: Although popular, firecrackers are being limited in some cities due to pollution.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hospitality – the friendly and generous reception and entertainment of guests.

p.em: Example: Diwali is famous for the warm hospitality shown by families to their neighbors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mythology – a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

p.em: Example: According to Hindu mythology, Diwali celebrates the return of Lord Rama.

cosy-blockquote.p: Feast – a large meal, typically a celebratory one.

p.em: Example: Families gather for a grand feast featuring traditional sweets and savory dishes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cleanse – to make something thoroughly clean.

p.em: Example: Many people cleanse and decorate their homes before the festival starts.

cosy-blockquote.p: Symbolism – the use of symbols to represent ideas or qualities.

p.em: Example: The symbolism of light in Diwali is universal across many different faiths.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why did lighting tiny clay diyas hold such a profound emotional significance when families were celebrating in the past?
★ Are there any multi-religious festivals in your country?

How did creating a colorful rangoli pattern reflect community spirit when neighbors were gathering outside?
★ Do you have any long multi-day celebrations in your culture?

Why did cultural ancestors place so much emphasis on wishing for financial and spiritual prosperity?
★ Do you usually clean your home before a big holiday?

What main ingredients turned a regular social gathering into a true public festivity last year?
★ What is the most common gift in your culture?

While people were setting off loud firecrackers, how did others discuss modern environmental concerns?
★ Do you prefer fixed dates or lunar dates for holidays?

Why was offering sweets and open-door hospitality considered a moral obligation during historical holidays?
★ Do you usually buy new clothes for special occasions?

How has ancient mythology shaped the modern-day rituals that our families had practiced for centuries?
★ Are there any "unusual" traditions in your family?

When families were preparing a grand communal feast, what was the ultimate way to foster reconciliation?
★ How do you welcome guests into your home?

Why did humans feel a deep psychological need to cleanse their physical spaces before the festival had even begun?
★ Does your favorite holiday have more than one name?

What was the universal symbolism of light conquering darkness, and why did it resonate so strongly in past centuries?
★ Which festival brings the most people together in your country?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: 🎨 Activity 1: The Rangoli Collaborative Masterpiece A Rangoli is a geometric floor design made to welcome guests. Together with your partner, choose the design elements, colors, and patterns for your communal Rangoli. Practice using narrative past tenses to describe the traditional patterns your families used to prepare: 🌀 Geometric Mandala Representing cosmic harmony, symmetry, and infinite prosperity. 🦚 Peacock Motif A vibrant symbol of grace, luck, and natural beauty. 🌸 Lotus Flower Base Symbolizing spiritual purity and a clean heart welcoming prosperity. 🪔 Closing: Feast of Light If you could light one symbolic Diya lamp today to bring light into one area of modern society, which would you choose to support? 📚 Lighting Global Education 🕊️ Securing International Peace 🌲 Restoring the Environment 🏠 Providing Homes & Welfare

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Traditional firecrackers will eventually be banned globally, which is what many environmentalists had predicted years ago.
★ Would you miss firecrackers if they were replaced by silent laser shows?

The intense commercialization of cultural holidays will eventually overshadow the ancient spiritual and mythology meanings that had guided previous generations.
★ Do you think gift-giving is the most important part of a mythology celebration?

In the future, virtual celebrations will replace the physical feast with family, which was taking place in-person for centuries.
★ Have you ever celebrated a grand feast from a culture that wasn't your own?

Global migration will lead to a world where different traditions merge, creating a new universal symbolism for light and hope that no one had anticipated.
★ Should your country have more public holidays for different religions to share their symbolism?

Wishing friends prosperity via instant messaging will replace the traditional act of sending physical greeting cards that families had cherished.
★ Do you prefer a physical card wishing you prosperity or a digital message?

Synthetic, mass-produced plastic decorations will eventually be outlawed, making people appreciate handmade art forms like rangoli that they had forgotten.
★ Do you value handmade art forms like rangoli more if you know they were made by hand?

The traditional practice to cleanse and prepare the home before holidays will be fully automated by domestic robots, replacing the manual effort we were doing.
★ How often do you cleanse your digital life of clutter?

Cultural fusion will become so prominent that traditional holidays will merge, creating globally shared moments of festivity that were developing slowly.
★ What is your favorite example of cultural fusion and shared festivity?

Physical diyas and oil lamps will eventually be replaced by interactive, high-tech LED projections, making real oil lamps something we had used only in history.
★ Why do humans find hope in the symbol of lighting traditional diyas?

In an increasingly individualistic world, extreme family hospitality that had characterized old communities will survive only as a paid professional service.
★ What is the most memorable act of hospitality a stranger has ever shown to you?

ul.li: Incorrect: It celebrate in India → Correct: It is celebrated in India ((Passive voice))
Incorrect: I am looking forward to visit India → Correct: I am looking forward to visiting India ((Looking forward to + -ing))
Incorrect: They give many gift → Correct: They give a lot of gifts ((Plural gifts))
Incorrect: I haven't saw the festival yet → Correct: I haven't seen the festival yet ((Present Perfect))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
